currentContext.business: GCL manufactures and markets Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC), converting Raw Petroleum Coke (RPC) — a by-product of petroleum refining — into value-added CPC or blends thereof. CPC is an essential raw material for the aluminium, steel, graphite, titanium dioxide and refractory industries, and the Company serves aluminium smelters, graphite electrode manufacturers, titanium dioxide producers and other metallurgical and industrial customers in India and overseas. Production is carried out at three plants in Goa, Paradeep (Odisha) and Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), supported by a manufacturing and distribution network across key industrial markets.

currentContext.mdna: Company outlook is closely linked to aluminium industry demand, supported by infrastructure development, urbanisation, electrification and growing adoption of lightweight materials|India expected to remain a key contributor to global aluminium demand growth on sustained infrastructure and manufacturing investment|Indian aluminium market expected to grow at a CAGR of around 7.6% through 2030 on favourable policy initiatives and industrial demand|India's per capita aluminium consumption of around 3.5 kg versus a global average of 12 kg indicates substantial headroom for demand growth|Global primary aluminium production projected at 74.39 million tonnes in FY2026 against consumption of 74.49 million tonnes — a marginal supply deficit that sustains carbon anode and CPC demand|CPC remains an indispensable input for carbon anodes used in aluminium smelting, so structural aluminium demand drivers translate into sustained CPC demand|Demand from the aluminium sector remained stable during FY2026 while domestic supply-demand imbalance pressured product realisations|Towards the close of FY2026 operating performance improved on better alignment of domestic product realisations with market conditions, timely raw material sourcing and supply chain optimisation|Planned maintenance shutdowns at the Goa and Bilaspur plants influenced production during the year|Regulatory framework (DGFT/CAQM import limits of 1.9 million MT of RPC for CPC manufacturers and 0.8 million MT of CPC for the aluminium industry) shapes raw material availability and cost structures|Industry remains exposed to green petroleum coke availability, energy costs, freight rates and evolving environmental regulations|Aluminium decarbonisation — renewable energy, recycling and energy-efficient smelting — is raising the premium on efficient operations, consistent quality and strong environmental practices among CPC manufacturers

risks.risk: Raw material sourcing and supply chain stability for Raw Petroleum Coke (RPC)
risks.note: RPC, the principal raw material for CPC, is sourced from both domestic and international markets; availability is influenced by global refinery output, evolving trade flows and international logistics. The IEA notes refinery operations and crude throughput are affected by changing feedstock availability, export restrictions and shifting trade patterns.

Geopolitical developments continue to affect global shipping routes and freight markets; UNCTAD reports disruptions in major maritime corridors have resulted in longer voyage distances, elevated freight costs and increased supply chain uncertainty.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange and interest rate exposure
risks.note: Dependence on imported RPC and the financing requirements of operations expose the Company to currency and rate risk — exchange rate moves influence the landed cost of imported raw materials while interest rate changes affect borrowing costs and finance expenses. Mitigated through currency hedging strategies and treasury practices.

risks.risk: Environmental regulation of petroleum coke import, production and use
risks.note: Aluminium is the largest consumer of CPC, requiring approximately 0.4 tonnes of CPC per tonne of aluminium produced, so any regulatory change affecting the import, production or use of CPC bears directly on the domestic calcination industry. The industry operates under stringent environmental regulation including regulated import quotas and prescribed emission standards.

risks.risk: Working capital and financing structure dependence on non-fund-based credit
risks.note: The Company relies primarily on non-fund-based facilities — sight and usance Letters of Credit, converted into Buyer's Credit through overseas banks backed by Trade Credit Bank Guarantees or SBLCs issued by Indian banks — to procure overseas raw material, making liquidity sensitive to credit line availability and financing terms.

Networks, systems, applications and data are exposed to external threats, damage and unauthorised access; the Company runs awareness and training programmes and cybersecurity risks are periodically reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board.
